surfaceForm: by user population (staff, student, contractor, visiting researcher)
proposedGenericDecision: Express endpoint populations as role categories the adopting institution defines, not a fixed four-member list; 'visiting researcher' presumes a research-intensive university shape.
rationale: The enumerated population set (staff/student/contractor/visiting researcher) encodes a research-university workforce model; a teaching-only college or a non-academic public body would have a different population taxonomy. The category 'visiting researcher' in particular is an implicit research-intensive assumption.

surfaceForm: a multi-OS estate combining Apple, Windows, Linux and mobile platforms across faculty boundaries
proposedGenericDecision: Replace 'across faculty boundaries' with a role-neutral organisational-unit term (e.g. 'across organisational units' or 'across administrative domains'); 'faculty' presumes a university faculty/department governance shape.
rationale: 'Faculty boundaries' is a university-specific organisational concept. An institution-agnostic infrastructure guide should refer to organisational units or administrative domains so the pattern reads for any large institution, not only a faculty-structured university.

surfaceForm: Linux endpoints --- typically present in research-computing environments even in Microsoft-centric institutions
proposedGenericDecision: Keep the operational observation but soften the universalising 'research-computing environments' assumption, which presumes a research-intensive institution; phrase as 'where present, e.g. research-computing or engineering environments'.
rationale: The clause assumes the adopting institution runs research-computing, which is a research-university trait. Mild implicit specificity; the underlying technical point (Linux managed via Ansible/osquery) is generic.

surfaceForm: Indicative duration is six to nine months for a moderate-sized institution.
proposedGenericDecision: Bind the duration estimate to a parameterised institution-size band rather than the unqualified 'moderate-sized', so adopters of different scale can recalibrate.
rationale: 'Moderate-sized institution' is an implicit scale anchor calibrated to a particular institution profile; durations (6-9, 12-18 months) are jurisdiction- and scale-bound estimates that should be presented as parameterisable bands, not constants.

surfaceForm: Jamf for Apple, Intune for Windows and Android, Ansible-and-osquery for Linux
proposedGenericDecision: Present product names as an illustrative example mix, explicitly marked as one possible instantiation, with the role abstraction (per-OS MDM/posture source) carried in the prose so the pattern is product-agnostic.
rationale: These are commercial/OSS product names, not institution identifiers; they are legitimate technology examples in an implementation guide. They bind the example to a specific toolchain but the surrounding text already frames the unified schema as the product-agnostic artefact. Keep, but ensure they read as exemplary not prescriptive.

surfaceForm: Jamf for macOS and iOS where present, Intune for Windows and Android, Ansible-and-osquery for Linux, possibly Workspace ONE in some segments
proposedGenericDecision: Same as the coexistence-section product list: keep as an explicitly illustrative product mix, abstraction carried by 'each existing endpoint-management product'.
rationale: Vendor names, not institution-specific. Legitimate as worked examples; flagged for completeness since they tie the pattern to a particular toolchain.

surfaceForm: Intune compliance signals ... Conditional Access expressions ... the equivalent OPA policies authored in Wave~4
proposedGenericDecision: Microsoft Intune / Conditional Access and OPA are specific products; keep as the named instantiation of the brownfield-Microsoft trajectory, which is by definition product-specific, but ensure the unified-schema abstraction remains primary.
rationale: This entire trajectory section is explicitly about Microsoft-centric estates, so the product naming is intentional and scoped. Not institution-specific. Low priority.

surfaceForm: their compliance signals are exported through OpenTelemetry collectors deployed during Wave~2
proposedGenericDecision: OpenTelemetry is an open standard rather than an institution identifier; keep as the canonical telemetry mechanism referenced suite-wide.
rationale: Open-standard tooling, suite-wide convention, not institution-bound. Listed only for completeness.

surfaceForm: Intune's iOS coverage is the working choice; there is no credible open-source alternative at scale at the time of writing
proposedGenericDecision: The OSS-gap acknowledgement is a generic market observation; keep the named product as the illustrative incumbent but frame the gap as a market condition (no credible OSS MDM for iOS at scale) rather than a recommendation of one product.
rationale: The named product is incidental to a generic sovereignty/OSS-gap point that holds for any institution. Not institution-specific. Keep.

surfaceForm: Patterns reported in NREN community fora and at EDUCAUSE
location: ul-it-policy/technical/ch24-wave6-endpoint-EN.tex, sec:w6-exit (realworldbox: Endpoint management at research-intensive institutions)
proposedGenericDecision: EDUCAUSE is a US/North-American higher-education association and NREN is a research-and-education-network concept; both presume a higher-education research context. Generalise to 'higher-education sector fora and NREN communities' or parameterise the named association for non-US adopters.
rationale: EDUCAUSE binds the precedent evidence to the North-American HE sector; an institution-agnostic guide adopted outside that region (or outside higher education) would cite a different sector body. The box title 'research-intensive institutions' also embeds a research-university assumption.

surfaceForm: Endpoint management at research-intensive institutions / Public documentation of endpoint architectures at large research-intensive institutions
proposedGenericDecision: Replace 'research-intensive institutions' with the role-based adopter term used suite-wide (e.g. 'the institution' / 'large institutions') so the guide does not presume a research-university adopter.
rationale: Repeated 'research-intensive institutions' framing narrows the document's implied audience to research universities. The infrastructure pattern is not intrinsically research-specific; the framing should be adopter-neutral.

surfaceForm: D-decision codes (D11.3, D11.6, D11.7, D12.2, D16.5, D17.3, D18.2, D24.1-D24.5) and \trchap cross-references
proposedGenericDecision: These are suite-internal decision identifiers and cross-reference macros, not institution-specific. They are part of the template machinery and should be retained as-is when the chapter is reused.
rationale: D-codes and \trchap{} are internal to the ITPOLICY suite's traceability scheme and contain no University-of-Luxembourg-specific terminology. They do not impede institution-agnosticism; flagged to confirm they were inspected and judged safe.

surfaceForm: GDPR Art. 32, NIS2 Art. 21(2)(g)/(i)/(j), ISO/IEC 27001 A.8.1/A.8.7/A.8.9, NIST CSF PROTECT (PR.PS)
proposedGenericDecision: GDPR/NIS2 are EU instruments and ISO/NIST are international standards; they are jurisdiction-broad rather than institution-specific. For non-EU adopters the EU instruments are an implicit jurisdiction assumption and could be parameterised against a local-equivalent register, but no national-transposition statement is made here.
rationale: No country is named and no national transposition is asserted; the anchors are EU/international frameworks applicable to any EU institution. Implicit EU-jurisdiction binding noted for completeness, but this is suite-wide policy, not chapter-local specificity. Keep unless the suite globally parameterises jurisdiction.

surfaceForm: the network-side BYOD posture verification ... is consistent with the institution's BYOD acceptable-use policy
proposedGenericDecision: Assumes the adopting institution maintains a BYOD acceptable-use policy. This is a reasonable role-based reference ('the institution's BYOD acceptable-use policy') and is already phrased generically; keep.
rationale: Already role-based ('the institution's ... policy') with no named institution. No change needed; confirms it was inspected.
